In the [[mathematical physics]] of [[quantum mechanics]], '''Liouville space''', also known as '''line space''', is the space of operators on [[Hilbert space]].  Liouville space is itself a Hilbert space under the [[Hilbert-Schmidt inner product]].<ref name=Chem /><ref name=Survey>{{cite journal|title=Fundamentals of quantum mechanics in Liouville space|first=Jerryman&nbsp;A.|last=Gyamfi|date=16 October 2020|journal=European Journal of Physics|volume=41|number=6|pages=063002|doi=10.1088/1361-6404/ab9fdd|arxiv=2003.11472|bibcode=2020EJPh...41f3002G }}</ref>  

Abstractly, Liouville space is equivalent ([[Isometric isomorphism|isometrically isomorphic]]) to the [[tensor product]] of a Hilbert space with its [[Continuous dual|dual]].<ref name=Chem>{{cite web|title=Hilbert space|url=https://www.chemie.uni-hamburg.de/nmr/insensitive/tutorial/en.lproj/hilbert_space.html|publisher=Uni Hamburg|archive-date=29 Oct 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029053526/https://www.chemie.uni-hamburg.de/nmr/insensitive/tutorial/en.lproj/hilbert_space.html|access-date=24 April 2022}}</ref><ref name=Open>{{cite journal|title=Elementary open quantum states|author1=Janos Polonyi|first2=Ines|last2=Rachid|journal=Symmetry|date=2021 |volume=13 |issue=9 |page=1624 |doi=10.3390/sym13091624 |arxiv=2106.01443v2|bibcode=2021Symm...13.1624P |doi-access=free }}</ref>  A common computational technique to organize computations in Liouville space is [[vectorization (math)|vectorization]].<ref name=Survey />  

Liouville space underlies the [[density operator]] formalism and is a common computation technique in the study of [[open quantum system]]s.<ref name=Survey /><ref name=Open />
